title: Night quicktrace cadence
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal runbook for night shifts — focused on fast triage and short-lived mitigations so morning shift has clear handover. Not a final playbook, just things that have worked for me in a pinch.

CURRENT SHIFT SUMMARY (2024-12-05 22:15 PT):
- No active Sev1s. Small blip earlier (21:05) where p95 token latency spiked to ~1.4s for ~12 minutes; auto-fallback to model-small succeeded.
- Ongoing: intermittent Redis connection errors reported by /cache/* path (seen in app logs ~5 times in last hour).
- Nightly quantize job scheduled at 02:00 — historically spikes GPU memory usage; keep an eye.

OPEN ITEMS FOR NEXT ESCALATION: (if persists >30m)
- Notify Diego (pager) -> escalate to Priya if rollback needed.
- If Redis errors > 10/min, trigger failover to read-only replica and open ticket PROD-4132.

QUICK CHECKS (first 5 mins):
- k8s: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep runtime
- runtime logs: kubectl -n inference logs deploy/redwood-runtime -c inference --since=15m | tail -n 200
- grep for: "KVCacheErr", "redis timeout", "OOM"
- metrics: open grafana -> cluster/inference -> Latency p50/p95/p99 and Token QPS
- redis: redis-cli -h redis-read.primary info keyspace | grep keys

IMMEDIATE MITIGATIONS (fast, reversible):
1) Redis connection storm:
  - Run: redis-cli -h redis-read.primary CLIENT LIST | wc -l  (if > 400, consider connection leak)
  - Flip proxy to replica: gcloud run-services update-proxy --service redis-proxy --force-readonly (this is a short-term step; document reasons)
  - Scale down worker pool that hits prefix-update endpoint: kubectl scale deployment prefix-updater --replicas=1
2) High token-latency showing CPU saturation on CPU nodes:
  - Enable temporary model-fallback route (applies to hosted API routing rules): curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/route-overrides -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","fallback":"model-small","duration":"30m"}' (use admin token)
3) GPU OOM during nightly quantize:
  - Kill quantize job early: kubectl delete job nightly-quantize-20241205
  - Reschedule with reduced batch-size: edit cronjob nightly-quantize -> set BATCH=16

ESCALATION CONTACTS (order):
- L1: Me (Maya Chen) — pager: +1-555-101-202 / slack: @maya
- L2: Diego Martinez — pager: +1-555-212-303 / slack: @diego
- L3: Priya Patel (runtime lead) — pager: +1-555-313-404 / slack: @priya
- On-call infra: Samir Gupta -> slack:#infra-oncall

HANDOVER CHECKLIST (what to leave for morning):
- Short description of what happened + exact time windows
- Commands run and outputs (paste clipped logs into ticket)
- Any config flips (routing, replica changes, flags) and reason
- Files changed: list PRs or patch ids and link them (e.g., PR#3421)
- Outstanding alerts to watch: token QPS, redis errors, quantize job memory.

EXAMPLE HANDOFF NOTE (paste into morning ticket):
- 22:05-22:17 PT: p95 token latency spike -> auto-fallback to model-small triggered by routing rules. Cause suspected: short-lived connection storm to Redis (see logs). Actions taken: scaled prefix-updater -> 1 replica; flipped redis proxy to read-only replica; monitored for 30 minutes; no further spikes.
- Next steps: confirm Redis repro with Priya and consider increasing connection pool limit. Linked: PROD-4132, PR#3421.

TOOLS / COMMANDS CHEAT SHEET (copy these into clipboard for quick use):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide
- kubectl -n inference logs deploy/redwood-runtime -c inference --since=30m | grep -i "redis\|kvcache\|OOM\|timeout"
- kubectl top pod -n inference | sort -k3 -nr | head
- prometheus query: rate(redwood_tokens_generated_total[5m])
- admin route override (see above)

KNOWN WEIRDNESS / TL;DR NOTES TO SELF:
- Prefetcher sometimes opens too many concurrent redis conns when warmup runs; symptom = lots of "client closed" in redis logs followed by timeouts. Quick fix: scale prefetcher to 1, then gradually increase.
- Model-small fallback increases API cost by ~15% but keeps p95 < 200ms. Worth it during noisy hours.
- Nightly quantize MUST be paused if GPU mem > 92% on any node prior to start.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS / FOR MORNING:
- Why did the connection storm happen? Look at deploys around 20:45 (was there a canary?). Link to commit: github.com/redwood/deploys/commit/ab12c3 (flagged).
- Should we add circuit-breaker on prefix-updater? Follow-up with Priya.

TODO (if you have time):
- Make tiny script to collect last 1h logs for infra-attest: /scripts/night-collect.sh (stub)
- Add grafana alert for redis client count > 350

FREE NOTES / scribbles:
- If fallback route repeated >3 times in 24h -> open regression eval for model change
- Keep an eye on SDK token expiration errors (seen once at 03:12 last week)
- REMEMBER: annotate the ticket with exact admin-token id used for overrides (security review)

-- end of quicktrace cadence scratchpad --
(If you copy/paste anything into shared docs, clean up shorthand and expand acronyms.)
